metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU, Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650. Quote: 'computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)'

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, used to calibrate simulation parameters and evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper explicitly states that the data used to support the results are available from the corresponding author upon request, with no public URL provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Final Result: DRL reduces average travel time by 13% vs no-control. Initial logic and parameters are validated. SUMO simulation environment is established using empirical data.

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed as the observation input
The fully connected layer in the Q-network in multitask learning is extended to two layers
The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/2 tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Leaping directly to final transformation. The trained DRL agent is evaluated against baselines and perturbed inputs to produce final metrics.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/2 tools named, all params stated

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Hyperparameters and RL setup are detailed, but the empirical traffic data used for SUMO calibration is closed (available upon request), preventing exact reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time series showing the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of vehicle travel times in the mainline for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation setup is described and SUMO is open-source, but the underlying empirical data for calibration is not publicly available.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean travel times across 20 simulation experiments with different random seeds for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear comparison across 20 runs, but requires exact simulation setup and proprietary empirical data to reproduce exactly.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing mean speeds across time and distance for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visualizes simulation outputs cleanly. Limited only by the availability of the empirical calibration data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time series of the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of queue lengths at the on-ramp for the three evaluated scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly plots simulation outputs. Reproducibility bounded by upstream simulation setup and closed empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time) in each simulation
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots showing the correlation between queue length and red ratio for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear methodology for extracting metrics from the simulation, but relies on unavailable empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Time series comparing queue length and downstream occupancy for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plots standard simulation metrics. Same upstream data limitations apply.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Boxplots of downstream traffic volume over time for the three evaluated scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear aggregation of simulation outputs. Reproducibility depends on the underlying SUMO setup and closed data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Boxplots showing travel times under different input data perturbation scenarios (removing subareas).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation method is described clearly, but relies on the same unavailable empirical data for the baseline simulation.
